subject: Chemistry
central_question: How do metal ions bind ligands to form coordination entities with characteristic names, structures, isomerism, bonding, colour and applications?
in_scope_units: Werner’s theory, primary and secondary valences and experimental formulation of cobalt-ammonia compounds.
Definitions of coordination entity, central atom, ligand, denticity, coordination number, sphere, polyhedron and oxidation number.
Formulas and IUPAC nomenclature of mononuclear coordination compounds.
Structural and stereoisomerism: ionisation, hydrate, linkage, coordination, geometrical and optical isomerism.
Valence Bond Theory, hybridisation, geometry and magnetic behaviour.
Crystal Field Theory, octahedral and tetrahedral splitting, high-spin and low-spin complexes and colour.
Bonding in metal carbonyls and applications of coordination compounds.
banned_topics: Detailed periodic trends of transition metals, which belong to the d- and f-block chapter.
Full ligand-field molecular-orbital theory beyond the NCERT crystal-field treatment.
Organometallic catalytic cycles beyond the brief metal-carbonyl discussion.

known_pitfalls.claim: The number of ligands always equals the coordination number.
known_pitfalls.correction: Coordination number counts donor atoms directly bonded to the metal; a polydentate ligand contributes more than one.

known_pitfalls.claim: Primary and secondary valences in Werner’s theory are both ionisable.
known_pitfalls.correction: Primary valences are normally ionisable; secondary valences are non-ionisable and correspond to coordination number.
Four-coordinate complexes may be tetrahedral or square planar depending on metal, oxidation state and ligand field.

known_pitfalls.claim: A strong-field ligand always makes every complex diamagnetic.
known_pitfalls.correction: Magnetism depends on d-electron count, geometry and splitting magnitude; strong fields favour pairing only when energetically favourable.

known_pitfalls.claim: Optical isomerism requires a carbon stereocentre.
known_pitfalls.correction: Coordination complexes can be chiral through their three-dimensional ligand arrangement even without an asymmetric carbon.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with NCERT Example 5.1 on secondary valences from AgCl precipitation.
Use NCERT Examples 5.2 and 5.3 for formula writing and IUPAC naming.
Use NCERT Examples 5.4–5.6 for geometrical and optical isomerism.
Apply NCERT Example 5.7 to magnetic moment and VBT/CFT reasoning.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter Exercises are numbered 5.1 to 5.31 and cover Werner’s postulates, terminology, nomenclature, isomerism, VBT, CFT, colour, magnetism, carbonyl bonding and applications.
